equipment_type: Water-cooled magnetic-bearing centrifugal chiller (via SC-EQ card)
applies_to: YORK YZ water-cooled magnetic-bearing centrifugal chillers (variable speed drive) fitted with the SC-EQ communication card.
summary: The YZ's SC-EQ card puts the chiller on a BACnet MS/TP trunk (it also speaks Modbus RTU and N2). The BAS can run/stop the chiller and write the leaving chilled liquid setpoint, input current limit and heating setpoint. Read-only points cover water temperatures, refrigerant pressures, VSD and harmonic filter values, magnetic bearing (MBC) mode, purge data, and operation, fault, warning and inhibit codes as MV objects with matching AV copies.
notes: Access is inferred: the sheet has no read/write column. The remote block (AV 1-3, BV 1) is treated as commandable and MV 65001 as writable; everything else as read-only.

Status-code MVs (operation, safety, cycling, warning, modified run, start inhibit, internal fault) are the printed code + 1, as the doc's status code tables say; the AV copies (AV 52-59) carry the raw code. MVs with their own enum in the points table are shown as printed; BACnet multistate values start at 1, so the card may report the printed number + 1. Confirm by discovery.
Harmonic filter, heat recovery, heat pump, hot gas bypass and dew point points only report when that option is fitted or enabled.
Units shown are the IP units; with MV 65001 set to SI the card reports °C, kPa and so on.
Spare objects (AV 4, BV 2-4 and the empty rows) are left out.

integration.summary: Wire the BAS to the SC-EQ J12 RS-485 port and set the MAC address; the card detects BACnet MS/TP. Run/stop the chiller with BV 1 and write the leaving chilled liquid setpoint (AV 1) and input current limit (AV 2). Read MV 1 for the operating state, BV 5 for motor run, the leaving water temperature and % FLA, and MV 2/MV 3 for safety and cycling shutdowns. MV 5 and MV 12-15 show whether the chiller is taking its commands from the BAS.

minimum_points.name: UNIT CONTROL SOURCE
minimum_points.why: Control source; BAS for BMS control

integration.enable: BV 1 REM RUN STOP CMD (0 = Stop, 1 = Run) is the BAS run/stop and AV 1-3 are the remote setpoints. MV 5 shows the unit control source (Local, BAS, Analog, Digital, Remote); MV 12 shows the run/stop source (Local, BAS, Hardwire) and MV 13-15 the cooling setpoint, heating setpoint and current limit sources. Check they read BAS. The points list has no write-enable point.
setup: The BAS connects to the SC-EQ J12 port (RS-485: +, -, COM/REF, SHLD). The card detects BACnet MS/TP, Modbus RTU or N2 and the baud rate by itself; allow up to 120 seconds after power-up.
The MAC address (1-127) is set on DIP switch SW1 (switch 8 unused). Cycle the card's power after changing it.

The device instance defaults to 5000 + the MAC address (MAC 6 gives 5006). To use another number, set Device Instance Mode to Manual and enter the instance with the SC-AP / MAP tool, or write BV 65000 (mode) and AV 65000 (instance ID).
MV 65001 Units sets whether the BAS sees IP or SI values, independent of the chiller display; set it to match the chiller.
gotchas: The remote (commandable) setpoints read as unreliable until the BAS writes them the first time.
The SC-EQ only exposes the points that apply to the chiller it detects; if it replaces an E-Link, re-discover the device so old non-applicable points don't sit offline.
Code points come in pairs: the MV state is the code + 1, and the AV copy (AV 52-59) carries the raw code.
